# Interop fixtures

Fixtures and pyarrow-derived expectations used by `test/interop/` for the
v0.1.2 and v0.2.0 compatibility matrices. Total committed size is ~1.4 MB;
every individual file is under 1 MB.

## Sources and licenses

| Group | Origin | License | Files |
|---|---|---|---|
| `official/` | [apache/parquet-testing](https://github.com/apache/parquet-testing) at commit `3acde70509f990c4ddfe34bf3ab05890657e766c` (2026-10-14), original `data/` layout flattened | Apache-2.0 (see [`LICENSE-parquet-testing.txt`](LICENSE-parquet-testing.txt)) | 59 (57 `.parquet`, 2 `.parquet.encrypted`) |
| `bad_data/` | same repository, `bad_data/` | Apache-2.0 | 5 malformed files |
| `generated/` | written by pyarrow / parquet-cpp-arrow 26.0.0 with [`tool/interop/make_pyarrow_fixture.py`](../../tool/interop/make_pyarrow_fixture.py): 11 rows, 4 row groups, flat+nested+UUID, DataPage v1 and v2 | MIT (this repository) | 2 |
| `v0.2/` | same parquet-testing commit: `shredded_variant/` cases 005/006/044/047/048/049/050/130 and `data/alp_extended.zstd.parquet`, with pyarrow-derived expectations and a v0.2 manifest | Apache-2.0 | 8 Variant Parquet + 8 `.variant.bin` + 1 ALP Parquet + expected JSON + manifest |
| `expected/` | generated by pyarrow 26.0.0 with [`tool/interop/gen_expected.py`](../../tool/interop/gen_expected.py) | MIT (derived data) | 67 JSON |

The subset was fetched over plain HTTPS with
[`tool/interop/fetch_parquet_testing.ps1`](../../tool/interop/fetch_parquet_testing.ps1)
(no git/gh clone). Pass `-Verify` to re-check every file against the SHA-256
hashes recorded in [`expected/manifest.json`](expected/manifest.json) and
[`v0.2/manifest.json`](v0.2/manifest.json).

## v0.2.0 assets (Variant / ALP / deep nesting)

See [`v0.2/README.md`](v0.2/README.md) for selection rationale, decoder-support
matrix and reproduction steps. Highlights:

- **Variant**: the smallest upstream cases — unshredded (`case-047`/`048`/`049`/
  `050`, 864–872 B), least-shredded primitives (`case-005`/`006`, 1152–1179 B)
  and shallow/nested shredded objects (`case-130`, `case-044`). Semantic
  expectations come from upstream `cases.json` plus the `.variant.bin` payloads;
  pyarrow reads only the physical struct, DuckDB and Polars reject the VARIANT
  logical type.
- **ALP**: `alp_extended.zstd.parquet` (218,992 B ≤ 1 MB) with FLOAT/DOUBLE
  PLAIN-reference and ALP-encoded columns. pyarrow/DuckDB/Polars cannot read the
  ALP columns; expected values are derived from the in-file PLAIN references.
  The v0.2 Dart reader already decodes all six ALP columns bit-exactly,
  including NaN payloads and nulls.
- **Deep nesting**: the five existing nested fixtures already present in
  `official/` each have a manifest entry with SHA-256, current typed error and
  the v0.2 target.

Fixture JSON documents (`expected/*.json`) record the file SHA-256, pyarrow
version, writer origin, leaf schema (`path`, physical type, type length,
logical kind, max definition/repetition level, decimal scale/precision),
per-column canonical value checksum, null count and sample values.

## Canonical value encoding and checksums

Python ([`tool/interop/interop_canon.py`](../../tool/interop/interop_canon.py))
and Dart ([`tool/interop/interop_canonical.dart`](../../tool/interop/interop_canonical.dart))
implement the same encoding:

- `null`, booleans and signed integers are JSON scalars;
- `FLOAT`/`DOUBLE` are raw IEEE bit patterns as `{"f32": "<8 hex>"}` /
  `{"f64": "<16 hex>"}` (bit-exact, including `-0.0` and NaN payloads);
- half floats, FLBA, INT96 and binary values are `{"hex": "..."}`;
- UTF-8/JSON/ENUM `BYTE_ARRAY` columns are strings;
- lists are JSON arrays; maps are `[[key, value], ...]` sorted by canonical key;
- structs are JSON objects with lexicographically sorted field names;
- a column checksum is FNV-1a 64 over `canonical_json(value) + "\n"` for every
  row.

This makes the checksum independent of JSON number formatting and stable across
Python and Dart. Maps/structs avoid ordering ambiguity; float bits avoid NaN
round-trip differences.

## Regenerating

```powershell
# optional: refresh the upstream download + verify hashes
pwsh tool/interop/fetch_parquet_testing.ps1 -Verify

# regenerate the pyarrow writer-origin fixtures (committed)
.agents/venv/Scripts/python.exe tool/interop/make_pyarrow_fixture.py

# regenerate expected/*.json from the committed fixtures
.agents/venv/Scripts/python.exe tool/interop/gen_expected.py
```

## Expected outcomes / known gaps

`kind: "values"` fixtures are read value-exactly and compared against pyarrow.
`kind: "manual"` fixtures have hand-written expectations because pyarrow cannot
decode them:

- `flba12_timestamp.parquet`: `FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY(12)` + `TIMESTAMP`; pyarrow
  rejects it. The raw 96-bit little-endian words are derived from the values
  documented in `data/flba12_timestamp.md`.
- `incorrect_map_schema.parquet`: pyarrow rejects the map schema; the reader
  accepts it leniently (as Presto-written files exist in the wild) and the one
  map row is pinned.
- `int96_from_spark.parquet`: rows 0鈥? come from the documented microsecond
  values; row 5 stores an out-of-range INT96 (negative Julian day/nanos) that
  pyarrow/DuckDB/Polars wrap or saturate, so its literal bytes are pinned.

`kind: "unsupported"` fixtures must throw `ParquetUnsupportedException`
(or `ParquetFormatException` for the MAP-without-value shape). They are the
documented v0.1.2 limitations: list-of-list, map-in-list/deep struct nesting,
bare repeated fields, MAP without value, encrypted files. `kind: "malformed"`
must throw a `ParquetException` subclass. See
[`test/interop/official_unsupported_test.dart`](../../test/interop/official_unsupported_test.dart).

## Notes

- The subset intentionally omits large parquet-testing files
  (`alltypes_tiny_pages_plain`, `large_string_map.brotli`, ALP/geospatial and
  Variant payload cases) to keep the repository small; Variant columns are
  physically readable as BYTE_ARRAY/FLBA but the Variant logical semantics are
  out of scope for v0.1.2.
- `bad_data/variants/*` files are valid Parquet carrying invalid *Variant*
  payloads; they are not malformed Parquet and are not included.
